newsitem.title: ITALY: Bertinotti says Italy must press on with budget.
newsitem.headline: Bertinotti says Italy must press on with budget.

text.p: The leader of Italy's hard-left Communist Refoundation party said the parties with a majority in parliament must press on with determination in approving 1997 budget legislation.

Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti defended the government's insistence on having special powers on tax reforms in the budget legislation after the Freedom Alliance opposition and the separatist Northern League said they would not participate in voting on the bill.
The government has asked parliament to give it numerous special powers to dictate policy on key budget areas, including tax reform, through so-called delegate laws.
A delegate law is one by which parliament gives the government a free hand to draft legislation within pre-defined limits without constantly referring back to parliament.
Bertinotti said: "It is not true that the delegate laws give the government unlimited powers."
"The new regional tax reform, for example, is aimed at combatting tax avoidance and evasion. We will not allow you to impede it," he told the Chamber of Deputies or lower house.
"You were not really interested in having a discussion, you really wanted the impossible," Bertinotti told the centre-right Freedom Alliance after it announced it would not participate.

Dialogue on the budget and use of delegate laws broke down over the weekend and centre-right leader Silvio Berlusconi announced earlier on Monday the Freedom Alliance would not take part in the voting process.

Bertinotti, whose party does not form part of the ruling centre-left Olive Tree coalition but whose support is vital to the government in the lower house, said: "This majority's job is to approve the budget...to press on with reforms and it must do so with great determination."

The deadline for approving the budget in the lower house has been put back to Sunday, November 17 from Thursday, November 14 originally. Once it has been approved by the lower house it passes to the Senate, where the centre-left Olive Tree coalition has an outright majority.
The entire package, which aims to lop 62.5 trillion lire from Italy's 1997 budget deficit, must be approved by December 31.
